note: All 122 findings after merging, with full reviewer details. Verification results for 62 of them are in findings.json; the other 60 were not verified.

findings.title: Saving silently stops working after roughly 40 turns: a 10-turn chunk document outgrows the 256 KiB db limit
findings.summary: Every stored turn embeds stateBefore, stateAfter, memBefore (a full copy of the memory incl. up to 600 events), pendingBefore and all regenerated alts; persist() writes 10 turns per document, so a chunk grows past 262,144 bytes and set() rejects invalid_argument. Transformation tracks keep their full drawn step texts in state.tf.tracks and every turn clones the whole state twice, which brings the failure forward to turn ~20 (or ~10 with six tracks).
findings.scenario: A player reaches turn ~40 in one adventure (turn ~20 in Sundered once three species tracks are alive, turn ~10 with six tracks); every later turn fails to save; closing the tab or opening on another device loses all progress after the last good save; dirty flag stays set so the page also keeps offering conflicts. The only user-visible signal is the small Summary-panel note.
findings.evidence: Lead probe (probe2.js, strict mock, 380-word narratives, 3 events/beats per turn): chunks 126K, 196K, 243K KiB at turns 10/20/30; turn 39 -> save failed: invalid_argument, violation doc-too-large adventures/<id>/turns/0003 is 266688 bytes (cap 262144). probe_st_24 (tracks): turn 20 save failed, chunks 202K/256K, doc-too-large turns/0001 294873 bytes; probe_st_25 (6 species): turn 10 save failed, turns/0000 275768 bytes. Code: tracks.push({... steps: drawSteps(content.steps) ...}) 1016; stateBefore/stateAfter: clone(state) 1544.
findings.repro: node C:/Users/marcu/AppData/Local/Temp/wl-harness/probe2.js (prints FIRST FAILURE turn 39); probes/probe_st_24.js and probes/probe_st_25.js
findings.fix: Store only what is needed per turn (drop memBefore/stateBefore or store diffs/hashes), keep track step texts out of per-turn snapshots (store indexes and look text up from world data), size chunks by bytes not by count of 10, and surface a persistent save-failed banner.

findings.title: Import writes only the last chunk of turns to the store, so an imported adventure loses its earlier turns on reload
findings.summary: importFile() builds a new adventure with all imported turns, then calls persist(), which writes the adventure doc and only the final 10-turn chunk. persistAll() (which writes every chunk) is not used.
findings.scenario: Player exports a 25-turn save, imports it (e.g. on another device or after deleting the original); the page looks right until reload/sync, then turns 1-10 are gone while turnCount still says 19.
findings.evidence: Lead probe (probe3.js): original adventure has chunk docs 0000,0001; imported copy has turnCount 19 but only chunk 0001 in the store.
findings.fix: Call persistAll(adv.id) after import (and verify with a read-back).

findings.title: An in-flight turn (or roommate intro) is committed into whichever adventure is loaded when the reply arrives
findings.summary: takeTurn, commitReply and writeRoommateIntro keep using the global adv/W after their awaits, but Continue, New adventure/Begin, Import, Delete-current and the boot load replace adv without checking busy (only #reloadAdv and #overwriteAdv check it, lines 2483-2484; setBusyUI disables only send/regen/regenWith/undo). The reply is applied to and persisted into the wrong adventure (processed under the other world's rules); a failed or stopped turn instead assigns its stateBefore to the other adventure (1608).
findings.scenario: Start a turn (30-120 s on the complex tier), open Adventures and press Continue on another save, or Import, or New adventure > Begin. When the reply lands it is pushed into the other adventure, its clock/state advance and it is saved there; the original never receives the turn, and a later Undo writes the foreign state into it. A roommate intro still being written after Begin goes to the new adventure with the OLD roommate's text. The same race exists at boot: a turn sent before db resolves lands in the freshly loaded save.
findings.evidence: probe_p5_2: A turns in store ['1:A first action','2:B SLOW action'], B keeps only turn 1. probe_c1_switch/_switch2: after the slow turn current adv B has A's action, store B turns/0000 holds it; new-adventure variant B clock 09:10 -> 09:25. probe_cr_3: new adventure B has 'SLOW ACTION FROM ADVENTURE A', turnCount 1; probe_cr_15: B gets A's roommate intro. probe_rend_4/_20, probe_p1_2 (sundered/halloway cross-world), probe_rt_3, probe_ps_6/_7 (S5-S7, H9a/b boot race), probe_ui_24/_35 all show the wrong-adventure commit; probe_p5_17: Undo writes Halloway state into the Sundered adventure.
findings.repro: probes/probe_p5_2.js, probe_c1_switch.js, probe_cr_3.js, probe_cr_15.js, probe_rend_4.js, probe_rend_20.js, probe_p1_2.js, probe_rt_3.js, probe_ps_6.js, probe_ps_7.js, probe_ui_24.js, probe_ui_35.js
findings.fix: Refuse (or disable the buttons for) Continue/New/Import/Delete/Begin while busy or while boot loading runs, and capture const mine = adv at the start of takeTurn/writeRoommateIntro and discard the commit and persist (and the rollback) if adv !== mine after any await.

findings.title: A failed Continue leaves the new world loaded over the old adventure; the next save stamps the wrong worldId and every turn errors
findings.lines: 1776-1790 (setWorld at 1780, before the chunk query at 1781), 1822, 1832, 1703 (advDoc worldId: W.id)
findings.summary: loadAdventure() calls setWorld(d.worldId) before the fallible chunk query and before adv is replaced, so a failure leaves W pointing at the other adventure's world while adv is still the previous one; no catch restores W. advDoc() writes worldId: W.id on the next persist.
findings.scenario: On a Halloway adventure the user clicks Continue on a Sundered save while the turns query fails (unavailable, rate_limited, malformed doc); the status says could not load, the header flips to The Sundered Isle, and the next turn dies with 'Page error while rendering'. Any Settings change or autosave rewrites the Halloway adventure with worldId sundered, so it later loads under the wrong world. The same happens when delete-current's follow-up loadAdventure fails.
findings.evidence: probe_tf_8b: stored B worldId = sundered with title 'Halloway College of Binding'; probe_tf_8: 'Page error while rendering: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading filter)'; probe_p5_3: header The Sundered Isle over the Halloway clock, turn not saved; probe_p1_10: store contains advmupw6uf7pd6f:sundered:Savemjj at Halloway College of Binding; probe_st_29: after failed load W.id = halloway while playing Mythaven, stored worldId = halloway; probe_ps_2: failed Continue leaves world title Sundered.
findings.repro: probes/probe_tf_8b.js, probe_tf_8.js, probe_p5_3.js, probe_p1_10.js, probe_st_29.js, probe_ps_2.js
findings.fix: Fetch the doc and chunks first, then call setWorld and assign adv together in one synchronous step (or restore the previous W in a catch). Apply the same ordering in importFile and newAdventure.

findings.title: Imported saves and stored docs are injected into innerHTML unescaped (stored XSS, zero-click at boot)
findings.summary: Numeric-looking fields (S.day, t.n, t.words, stateBefore/After.day, e.intensity, player.stats values, influence, attitudes, tf trait/sex/track day) are concatenated into innerHTML without esc(), while importFile()/loadAdventure() and the shared store accept any JSON for them; the Override dialog value= attributes are unescaped too.
findings.scenario: A victim imports a shared windlass-save-1 file (or another viewer writes an adventure doc with a newer updatedAt, which boot auto-loads as the newest save) whose state.day or turns[0].words is an img-onerror payload. It executes on render with no click, is persisted, and re-runs on every later load, with access to window.claude db, sample and downloads (read, rewrite or delete every save, spend the viewer's usage).
findings.evidence: '' + t.words + ' w' (2330); 'Day ' + S.day (2276); esc(W.stats[k]) + ' ' + p.stats[k] (2358); '' + v (2384); value=attributes at 2168. Real Chrome against the mock: imported turns[0].words img-onerror -> window.__pwned===1 and an in #feed; poisoned doc made onerror fire 48 (and 815) times and typeof window.claude.use was function. Override day payload gives #clock innerHTML 'Day 1'. jsdom probes: injected nodes in #feed, #clock, #attitudes, #stats (pwn4) and the transformation panel (pwn1-3); stored words value is the markup. jsdom does not run onerror in the probes.
findings.repro: probes/probe_rend_19.js, probe_sec_1.js, probe_sec_2.js (plain boot, no clicks: '#clock has img id=pwn: true'), probe_rt_5.js (c), probe_ui_9.js, probe_ui_11.js, probe_tf_9.js, probe_tf_9b.js; plus Chrome-pane runs on 127.0.0.1:4173
findings.fix: Wrap every interpolated value in esc() or Number() (or build these nodes with textContent), escape the Override value attributes, and validate/coerce numeric fields (day, n, words, intensity, attitudes, skills, stats, tf day) on import and on load.

findings.title: A failed chunk write is never repaired: history gaps, state ahead of the log, duplicate turn numbers, and a later 'saved' note hides it
findings.summary: persist() writes the adventure doc (state, memory, rev, turnCount) first and then only the 10-turn chunk containing the newest turn, so a rejected chunk write (K1 size cap, quota, transient unavailable, which is not retried once as the db contract asks) is never retried or backfilled. loadAdventure never compares turnCount with the turns it loaded, and turn numbers and chunk indexes are positional, so gaps and duplicates are propagated and the note flips back to 'saved'.
findings.scenario: (a) Once K1 rejects chunk 0003, chunk 0004 still saves, leaving turns 39, 40 missing while the doc says turnCount 48; (b) one transient unavailable on the write of turn 10 permanently drops that turn (reload shows 11 of 12 or 9 of 11). After a reload the next turn reuses an existing number (46 twice) and re-slices a chunk, permanently dropping turns 41-42.
findings.evidence: probe_rt_8: chunks 0003:31..38, 0004:41..47, main.turnCount 48, reload shows 45 turns, labels Turn 45,46,47,46; probe_rt_9: one unavailable on the turn-10 chunk write leaves 0000:1..9, later note reads saved, reload 13 of 14; probe_ps_4 S1/S2: chunk0 1..9 | chunk1 11,12, fresh boot 11 of 12, note 'saved'; probe_ps_12: first failure at turn 17, boot shows 16, store turnCount 17; probe_p5_8: after one more turn chunks 0004=43,44,45,46,47,46, turnCount 46, note saved.
findings.fix: Write the turn chunks before the adventure doc, remember failed chunk indexes and rewrite them on the next persist (retry unavailable once after a short random delay), keep a visible warning while dirty, warn/repair on load when turnCount differs from loaded turns, and derive turn.n from max(n)+1 and the chunk index from turn.n instead of array position.

findings.title: Prompt-size guard cannot shrink the largest sections and never re-checks its last step; long Sundered games dead-end with prompt_too_large
findings.summary: The guard only trims timeline events, older beats and the verbatim window, then sends the last candidate without measuring it. Lore (up to ~10K), characters (~8.5K), gm_only (~5K), transformation (~7K), facts (up to 60, ~10 KB) and summary are never reduced, and the memory fold runs only after a successful turn. Sundered's base prompt is already ~52 KB.
findings.scenario: Standard Sundered game with 3 facts of ~30 words per turn: the guard engages at turn 7 and turn 18 fails with 'Prompt too large ... lower the verbatim window', although the window is already forced to 1 and Settings offers only 2-4. Every retry fails; only emptying the summary or Undo gets out. Sundered with several kinds at influence >= 15 hits 66,073 bytes after the last guard step.
findings.evidence: Loop: for (const lim of [...]) { if (bytes(built.prompt) <= 63000) break; ... } (last build never measured). probe_eng_3 (DENSITY=standard WINDOW=3 NARR=450 FACTLEN=32): FAIL turn 18, 65,732 B (cap 65,536); probe_eng_5: status Prompt too large x3, injected late-game 68,147 B, 0 fold calls, facts block 10,319 B; probe_eng_4: 63,044 B at last limit with 60 facts, 68,457 B with all closed places found; probe_c1_late (KINDS=4): {window:1,events:10,earlier:6} -> 66,073 B; probe_c1_long4: prompt_too_large on every retry from turn 13 through 30.
findings.fix: Loop until the measured prompt fits, adding later shedding stages (older facts, summary, lore hard cap, exemplars, minor characters, GM fragments, tf lines), re-measure after the final stage, run the memory fold before the call when over budget, and reword the error to something the player can act on.

findings.title: Mythaven roommate intro hard-codes the template's name while the default roommate name is usually a generic one
findings.summary: rmNamesFor() appends the _generic name pool to every species and randomField('rmName') draws uniformly, so ~83% of default roommates get a generic name, but all nine authored intros hard-code the template surname (harpy also hard-codes 'Juniper'). Template roommates are never rewritten by writeRoommateIntro, so this text is the player-facing Turn 0.
findings.scenario: Mythaven goblin roommate Tobiah Renn says '"Brasswick," he says. "Tobiah."'; harpy Perpetua Ross says '"Juniper," she says. "Ashwing."'; cow Perpetua says '"Vega."'. Cast, state and memory name one person and the opening text another, and the narrator treats both names as established. A female cow roommate also removes Marisol via replaces whatever her name.
findings.evidence: probe_mw_3: every species/gender row 'suggested 6 | own-template names 1 | P(generic)= 0.83'; probe_mw_4 (name Perpetua Ross): all nine intros keep their own surname; probe_ph_5: 'mismatching roommate names: 22 of 27'; probe_ph_2: harpy Nova Pike gets 'Juniper... Ashwing'.
findings.fix: In rmNamesFor use only the matched template's names when a species matched; add a rm_last token to vars() and use it (and {rm_First}) in the intros, or use {rm_first}; apply replaces only when the roommate actually is that character.

findings.title: Failed import replaces the live adventure and world before validating, so a malformed save breaks the page and can poison the next boot
findings.summary: importFile calls setWorld and assigns adv from the file before checking that state, memory and turns exist; the world check WORLDS[wid] is truthy for inherited names such as constructor. The catch only shows 'Import failed', leaving a half-built unsaved adventure (and possibly another world) current.
findings.scenario: A hand-edited, truncated or other-version save without state/memory reports Import failed, but the old adventure is gone from memory; the next turn or render fails with 'Page error while rendering' until reload. A Settings change then persists a doc without state, and the next boot says 'Your saved adventure could not be loaded' because boot tries only the newest doc. A settings.narrTier of bogus imports fine and fails every turn.
findings.evidence: probe_p5_4: 'Import failed: ... reading tf', next turn 'Page error ... reading weekday'; probe_p1_9: 'Import failed ... reading facts' then 'Page error ... reading weekday', world title switched; probe_ui_10: Settings change stores a doc with no state key, reboot 'could not load saves: undefined is not valid JSON' (relies on mock dropping undefined fields); probe_sec_3: 8 malformed imports, worldId constructor gives empty #worldTitle; probe_sec_9: store doc with worldId constructor makes boot report 'could not be loaded'.
findings.repro: probes/probe_p5_4.js, probe_p1_9.js, probe_ui_10.js, probe_sec_3.js, probe_sec_9.js, probe_rt_5.js (b), probe_ps_8.js (IMP1/IMP2)
findings.fix: Build and validate the new adventure into locals (own-property world check, object-typed state and memory, array turns, tier whitelist) and call setWorld and assign adv only after validation succeeds, restoring the previous ones on failure; make boot fall back to the next-newest save and treat a doc without state as unloadable.

findings.title: Adventure id is taken from the doc body, not the document path: one doc can overwrite or delete another adventure
findings.summary: loadAdventure sets adv.id = d.id (body field) and listAdventures drives open/rename/delete from a.id (body), so a document whose body id names a different adventure redirects every later write and delete to that other adventure; nothing checks that body id equals the path id.
findings.scenario: Any store writer (or a damaged doc) creates adventures/other1 with body id equal to your adventure's id and a high rev; after boot auto-loads it, your next action persists to adventures/<your id> and replaces your save. Clicking Delete on the innocent-looking row removes your adventure doc and all its chunks.
findings.evidence: adv = { id: d.id, ... } (1784); db.doc('adventures/' + adv.id).set(doc) (1759); row delete uses a.id (1826). Observed: victim doc title became EVIL after one action (rev 999 bypasses newerInStore); after Delete on the Harmless row the victim doc and its chunks were gone.
findings.fix: Use the snapshot/path id everywhere and verify or ignore the body id; reject docs whose body id differs from the path.

findings.title: Saves, presets and recents live in shared top-level collections; boot opens the newest save written by any viewer
findings.summary: All data is written under root collections (adventures, presets, meta) shared by every viewer; only data/users/<id>/ is private. Boot loads orderBy(updatedAt desc).limit(1) of the shared collection and ignores the per-viewer windlass.last key; no use('user') or data/users path exists.
findings.scenario: Once the artifact is shared with a Contributor, their adventures appear in your list, your next launch opens whichever save was written last by either of you, 'Picked up the newer save from your other device' pulls in the other person's turns, two people playing hit the conflict banner, and either can continue, overwrite or delete the other's save; a view-only member sees every write rejected as a small 'save failed' note. A hostile save also reaches every viewer (see the XSS finding).
findings.evidence: db.collection('adventures').orderBy('updatedAt','desc').limit(1) (2567); persist writes adventures/<id> (1759); listAdventures 1814; presets 2130; meta/recent 1928; grep for data/users, use('user'), can('data finds nothing. Not verified against an actually shared copy or declared db rules.
findings.fix: Key a viewer's data under data/users/<id>/ (declare user, await user.id()) or declare db rules making adventures owner-only and gate controls with user.can; load the last-used save by id before falling back to the newest.

findings.title: Partial failures in copy, delete and undo leave truncated or corrupt records that look healthy in the list
findings.summary: persistAll writes the adventure doc (turnCount = N) before its chunks, delete removes chunk docs oldest-first before the adventure doc, and undo deletes the stale chunk last, with no rollback or cleanup; the copy handler only shows an error and never refreshes the list.
findings.scenario: Save a copy of a ~40-turn adventure hits K1 on a later chunk: the status says 'That did not work', but a copy doc claiming 40 turns exists with 3 chunks and opens with 30. An interrupted delete leaves the adventure listed as 25-35 turns but opening with 15; a failed copy leaves a listed copy with no turns; a failed chunk delete during undo means a reload resurrects the undone turn (shows 10, expected 9).
findings.evidence: probe_ps_9: COPY store copy doc turnCount 17, chunks 0000 only; DEL 'That did not work: unavailable', boot shows 15 of 25; probe_ps_4 S3: boot 10 expected 9; probe_ps_12 (copy under K1); probe_ui_20: after 40 turns copy doc turnCount 40 with 3 chunks vs original 4, list still 1 row; probe_p5_18: chunk 0002 delete fails, doc still listed 35 turns, opening shows 16 feed items.
findings.fix: Write chunks before the doc when copying (or delete the partial copy in a catch), delete the adventure doc first or mark it deleting, delete the stale undo chunk before rewriting, and trim loaded turns to turnCount with a warning on mismatch.

findings.title: Revision-based stale detection can be defeated: a failed save pre-bumps rev, and the doc is written before its chunk
findings.summary: persist() sets adv.rev to rev+1 before the write, so a failed save leaves this page claiming a revision the store never got. It also writes the adventure doc (new rev, turnCount) before the chunk, so a device that syncs in between adopts the new rev with the old chunk.
findings.scenario: A's save fails once (rev 5 held locally only); B then saves a genuine rev 5; A's next turn sees no newer save and silently overwrites B's turn. If B's focus/visibility/60 s sync lands between A's doc write and chunk write, B loads 'rev 5, 2 turns', never reloads, and its next turn overwrites the chunk, deleting A's turn.
findings.evidence: adv.updatedAt = doc.updatedAt; adv.rev = doc.rev; await db.doc(...).set(doc); ... await chunkRef(chunkIdx).set(...). probe_ps_13: B turn 3 present in store? false (failed-save case); probe_ps_14: 'Picked up the newer save (2 -> 2 turns)' then A turn 3 survived? false.
findings.fix: Assign adv.rev only after the write succeeds, write the chunk before the doc (or store the chunk revision in the doc), and reload when turnCount differs from the loaded turns.

findings.title: Other-device deletes and renames are invisible to an open page; its next save resurrects a truncated adventure or reverts the rename
findings.summary: newerInStore treats a missing adventure doc as 'nothing newer', so a page holding a deleted adventure silently re-creates it on its next persist, writing only the last 10-turn chunk. Renaming a non-current adventure does a bare set() with no rev/updatedAt bump, so a page holding it never notices and overwrites the new title.
findings.scenario: Device A deletes adventure X while B still shows it, then B takes a turn: X reappears in A's list as '13 turns' (26 in another run) but opens with only 3 (6), since earlier chunks were deleted. Renaming X on A while B has it open is silently reverted by B's next turn, with no conflict offered and nothing shown on focus.
findings.evidence: probe_p5_6: after B turn X doc? true turnCount 13 | chunks ['0001'] | turns in chunks 3; A opens X: 4 feed items (expected 14). probe_p5_7: store title 'X renamed on A' rev 3 -> after B turn 'Adventure X' rev 4. probe_ps_5: rename on B reverted after A takes a turn (rev 4 -> 5); delete: B store {turnCount:26, chunks:0002}, fresh page shows 6 turns.
findings.fix: Bump rev and updatedAt on rename via the same write path as persist; treat a missing doc for an adventure with adv.rev > 0 as deleted (stop saving and offer to restore via persistAll or discard).

findings.title: 'Save a copy' makes the copy the most recent save and mutates the live adv.title across awaits, so a racing save renames the original
findings.summary: The copy's updatedAt is newer than the adventure being played, and boot opens the most recently saved adventure; the copy handler also swaps the live adv.title across the awaits of persistAll(newId), so a double-click on OK or any persist() (a turn finishing, a settings change) serialises the temporary title and renames the original.
findings.scenario: A player saves a backup copy before a risky choice and closes the tab; on reopen (or another device) the page loads the copy and play continues there with nothing in the main view showing the title. With a racing save, or a double-click on OK, both docs (or two copies) end up titled '... (copy)'.
findings.evidence: probe_p5_13: after copy + reload the open adventure is ['Backup copy [Current]','Played One [Continue]']; with a racing save original doc title in store after copy+racing save: THE COPY; probe_rend_11 (db 40 ms): double OK -> 2 copies, original title became '... (copy)' after next save.
findings.fix: Pass the title into persistAll instead of mutating adv.title, give the copy an updatedAt at or below the source's so the source stays the latest save, and disable OK while the copy is being written.

findings.title: persist() returns nothing, so callers announce success after a failed or refused save, and conflict banners are overwritten
findings.summary: persist() swallows errors and conflicts and returns undefined. Cast Save, Override edits, Add fact and Import then show 'Saved.', 'Fact added.' or 'Imported ...' regardless, and a status line set afterwards replaces the conflict banner.
findings.scenario: With the db down, Cast Save shows 'Saved.', Add fact 'Fact added.', and Import 'Imported X (imported).' although nothing reached the store. On a stale page Add fact makes persist() offer the conflict, then setStatus('Fact added.') wipes the banner (no buttons) and the save note stays 'loaded'.
findings.evidence: renderAll(); ... await persist(); $('#cfNote').textContent = 'Saved.'; await persist(); setStatus('Fact added.'). probe_ps_10: 'A cast: cfNote = Saved. | save note = save failed: unavailable'; 'A import: status = Imported ... | adventures in store: 1'; 'B fact add on stale page: status = Fact added. | buttons: 0'.
findings.fix: Make persist() return true/false (or throw) and announce success only on true; keep the conflict banner from being replaced by routine status text.

findings.title: A failing save, db-unavailable and export fallback are signalled only in the Summary panel's small note, which phones keep closed
findings.summary: setSaveNote() writes 'saved', 'save failed', 'no saves yet' and 'saves unavailable in this view' into #summaryNote inside the Character rail, which is display:none at <=900px; there is no banner, header indicator or retry. When db is unavailable the Adventures dialog still says 'Every turn is saved automatically', and a downloads fallback dumps raw JSON with no heading, instructions or Copy button.
findings.scenario: After K1's invalid_argument (or quota/unavailable), a phone player keeps taking turns that are never stored and closing or reloading loses everything since the last good save; on a db-less view they play a long session with no banner; with downloads=0, Export fills the dialog with 168 KB of unexplained JSON (12 turns) whose 'copy the text below' hint sits behind the dialog.
findings.evidence: probe_rend_17 (mobile, every adventure-doc set rejected): #status hidden, header 'Claude ready', only #summaryNote 'save failed: invalid_argument' inside #rail; feed 2 turns, stored turnCount 0. Browser 375px: getComputedStyle(rail).display none, summaryNote.offsetParent null, rect 0x0. ?db=0: #status '' and #summaryNote 'saves unavailable in this view'; ?downloads=0: #exportFallback.textContent.length 168255, #dbNotice empty.
findings.repro: probes/probe_rend_17.js; Browser pane 375x812 on http://127.0.0.1:4173/ (also ?db=0 and ?downloads=0)
findings.fix: On persist failure or missing db show a persistent bad status banner (or header pill) with Retry until a save succeeds; give the export fallback a heading, instructions and a Copy/select-all button inside the dialog; reword line 315 when db is null.

findings.title: Export filename .slice(0, 80) cuts off '.json', so long titles always fail with rejected_extension and fall into a JSON dump
findings.summary: (W.id + '-' + slug + '.json').slice(0, 80) removes the extension whenever the slug exceeds about 65 characters, which downloads.save rejects with rejected_extension; the catch then dumps the whole JSON into #exportFallback for any non-'declined' error (including rate_limited from a double click) with the generic 'download unavailable' note, and the pre is never hidden again. Non-Latin titles collapse to 'sundered--.json'.
findings.scenario: A player renames an adventure to a descriptive 70-90 character title (or imports a save, which appends ' (imported)') and presses Export: no download prompt appears and a multi-KB (59-168 KB) JSON dump fills the dialog; a later successful export leaves the stale dump of the earlier adventure visible.
findings.evidence: probe_p5_5: 72-char title -> violation download-extension, fallback shown, note 'download unavailable'; 'Short title' and a Japanese title save as sundered-short-title.json and sundered--.json. probe_rt_5 (a): 90-char title, fallback pane 59,667 chars; probe_ps_8 (H2): 90-char title, downloads [] and note shown; probe_ui_12: 70-char fails, 66-char saves; probe_sec_7 and probe_p1_11 likewise.
findings.repro: probes/probe_p5_5.js, probe_rt_5.js (a), probe_ps_8.js, probe_ui_12.js, probe_sec_7.js, probe_p1_11.js
findings.fix: Slice the slug (to about 60 chars) before appending '.json'; fall back to the text dump only for unavailable/not_granted, tell the player to retry on rate_limited, show the failure inside the dialog, and hide #exportFallback on success.

findings.title: The transformation block grows without bound and the size guard cannot shrink it: turns fail with prompt_too_large once all ten kinds are complete
findings.summary: bodyNowLines emits each completed kind's finished shape plus, for every path other than tf.sex.species, all its 'Toward a woman's body so far' lines on every prompt. takeTurn's guard only trims events, older beats and the verbatim window.
findings.scenario: Sundered with 10 kinds complete: block is 15,489 B (3,155 B with none), the prompt is 67,512 B against the 65,536 cap, and the turn fails with the useless advice to lower the verbatim window (already at 1). With 9 kinds the prompt is 64,664 B after every reduction; without the stale sex lines the same state fits at 62,898 B.
findings.evidence: Per kinds complete: 9 -> 64664/ok, 10 -> 67512/prompt_too_large; section bytes transformation 15489. With path.sex null for all kinds: 10 -> 62898/ok.
findings.repro: probe_tf_7.js (sweep 0-10 kinds), probe_tf_7b.js (no sex paths), probe_tf_6.js (section sizes)
findings.fix: Emit only the finished-shape line for completed kinds and drop sex lines once tf.sex is set; let the guard remove the tf lines as a last resort.

findings.title: 'Previous version' restores an already advanced state but clears the engine notes, so a started change, arc phase or progression note is never narrated
findings.summary: usePreviousVersion restores prev.stateAfter, whose track indexes, arc phases and spa/progression flags are already advanced, but sets adv.pendingNotes = [] because turn records keep only pendingBefore. The alts list is also rewritten so only the two newest versions can be reached.
findings.scenario: The player regenerates the turn that began a wolf change and clicks Previous version: the next prompt has no engine note, yet the transformation block lists step 0 as told, so the step is silently skipped (the world rules say never skip one); the same loses arc phases, Spa-return and progression notes. With three versions the button reads 'Previous version (2)' but only toggles between versions 2 and 3.
findings.evidence: adv.pendingNotes = [] (1697); prev.alts = t.alts.concat([cur]) (1694). probe_tf_3: turn 3 prompt engine notes = [] next to 'Under way (...), told so far'; probe_eng_9: v1 pendingNotes 1 ('A change is beginning...'), after Previous version [] with tracks i:1, next prompt contains 'Note from the engine': false; probe_st_6: pending notes 0; probe_st_18: visits 2 -> 3 -> 2 -> 3 -> 2, v1 unreachable.
findings.fix: Store pendingAfter on each turn record and restore it here; keep alts as an ordered list with a current index instead of popping and re-pushing.

findings.title: A second sex path is rolled, announced and finished on a body that is already a woman's; spa reset of one kind erases the other's result
findings.summary: manifestDue rolls the sex change from the player's declared gender only, never from tf.sex or other active paths; advanceTracks overwrites tf.sex with whichever path finishes last (tf.sex records a single species), and the spa reset deletes tf.sex by species.
findings.scenario: A male or non-binary player completes the harpy path (chance 1), tf.sex is harpy; a later wolf or cow path rolls female again, the narrator is told twice that the body 'has finished going over' (although the note says to say it once), bodyNowLines keeps 'Toward a woman's body so far' for a female body, and tf.sex flips to wolf. A Spa reset of wolf alone deletes tf.sex and queues 'the body's sex is as it was' although harpy is at 100 and finished.
findings.evidence: probe_tf_4b: turns 40-41 'Alongside the werewolves change, the body is going toward a woman's', then 'finished going over (werewolves path)'; after spa reset of wolf: no woman's-now line and harpies back to 'Toward a woman's body so far'. probe_tf_1: two concurrent sex tracks announce 'finished going over' at prompts 31 and 36. probe_st_7: T35 'body is a woman's now (cow path)', T40 '(wolf path)', final tf.sex wolf; probe_st_23: after spa_reset [wolf] tf.sex = null, cow rungs 5 with path.sex female, pending note 'sex is as it was'.
findings.fix: Skip the roll and sex tracks when tf.sex is already set (or another path carries sex), set tf.sex only if absent (keep sex as a body-level fact with contributing species), and recompute it from remaining finished paths on spa reset.

findings.title: 'Body now' drops the sex lines already told for a rung when its sex track ends, until the body track settles
findings.summary: Told sex lines are rebuilt from ladder[i].sex only for i below the settled body-trait count plus the live sex track. The 1-2 step sex track ends and is removed several turns before the 5-9 step body track settles, so neither source lists them in between.
findings.scenario: For a male player the jaw and voice lines are told at prompts 10 and 12, then prompts 12-15 carry no 'Toward a woman's body so far' line and it returns only at prompt 16; the narrator's continuity block omits established facts and may contradict them.
findings.evidence: Observed werewolves lines per prompt: 10-11 Toward lines present; 12-15 absent while the body track is under way; 16+ present again.
findings.repro: probe_tf_1.js, output in out_tf_1.txt (awk over 'Body now (werewolves)' lines)
findings.fix: Record told sex lines on tf.paths[k] (or per-rung finished flags) and list them independently of body settling.

findings.title: List items silently drop the newest entries once maxItems is reached (Discoveries caps at 12, inventory at 20)
findings.lines: 860-863 (863: slice(0, def.maxItems || 30)); worlds/sundered.js:794-797 (discoveries maxItems 12 at 797); worlds/mythaven.js:524-526
findings.summary: applyUpdates concatenates an append and then slices from the front, so once a list is full every new entry is discarded with no engine note and no diff entry. Sundered caps discoveries at 12, romances/clubs/wearing at 8 and inventory at 20.
findings.scenario: A long game logs finds with append; after the 12th, later finds (the Glass Orchard, the cold larder, endgame finds) never appear in the Discoveries row or the narrator's <state>, so the narrator keeps re-adding them; a 13th discovery, ninth gift or 21st item is never stored although the model believes it recorded it.
findings.evidence: probe_st_31: 14 appended discoveries -> length 12, last kept 'discovery 12', has 'discovery 14'? false, notes [] diff []; probe_st_1: full inventory of 20 + append 'THE NEW SWORD' not present; probe_sw_7: Discoveries held exactly 12 entries after 14 appends.
findings.fix: Keep the newest entries (slice(-max)) or raise discoveries to ~30, and push an engine note whenever anything is trimmed.

findings.title: Any state_updates op other than set/inc/append/remove silently becomes 'set', wiping lists
findings.summary: The op is read with String(u.op || 'set').toLowerCase() and every unrecognised value falls into the set branch with no note, so for lists and 'present' the whole value is replaced by the new entry.
findings.scenario: A model that writes op 'add', 'push', 'delete', 'drop' (or 'append ' with a space) on inventory or present replaces the whole list with the single value ('delete' makes the removed item the only entry); on number items 'dec' with value 1 sets the item to 1.
findings.evidence: probe_st_21: op add 'a rope' -> inventory ['a rope'], present ['Dean Marrow'], notes []; same for push/delete/drop/'Append '/insert. probe_st_31: inventory after {op:add,value:'a coil of rope'} = ['a coil of rope']. probe_st_1: reach_salt op dec 1 on 4 -> 1.
findings.fix: Trim and validate op against the four allowed values (optionally map add/push to append, delete/drop to remove, dec to negative inc); for anything else add an 'ignored unknown op' note and skip.

findings.title: Override and Cast edits made during a running turn are silently reverted when that turn fails or is stopped
findings.summary: overrideApply() and saveCast() mutate adv.state without checking busy; takeTurn's catch then restores its pre-turn snapshot (adv.state = stateBefore), wiping those edits while the UI and the store had already reported them as saved.
findings.scenario: While a slow turn is pending the player sets an attitude in Override (status 'Override: attitude roommate = 9.', persisted); the turn then fails (upstream_error) or is stopped and memory reverts to 7; the next persist overwrites the store with 7. A Cast Save of attitude or a rename (which rewrites state.present) is lost the same way.
findings.evidence: probe_cr_19: roommate attitude before 7 / override applied during turn 9 / status after failed turn 'The service failed mid-turn.' / attitude after failed turn (expected 9): 7. No busy check in overrideApply (2173) or saveCast (2208).
findings.fix: Disable the Override and Cast controls (or make them wait) while busy, or apply the rollback by diffing rather than replacing adv.state wholesale.

findings.title: A save during Regenerate writes the popped turn list; a failed or stopped regenerate leaves the store one turn short while the page says 'saved'
findings.summary: onRegenerate pops the last turn and rewinds state and memory before the model call, and persist() (called by any settings change, summary save, cast edit or Override) serialises that intermediate state. A failed or stopped regenerate restores memory in the page but never re-saves.
findings.scenario: Press Regenerate, change the narration tier while it waits, and the regenerate fails or is stopped: the page shows 3 turns and 'saved', the store has turnCount 2, so a reload or other device loses the last turn until the next save; a summary edit made during the wait is also silently reverted in the page.
findings.evidence: Observed: before store turnCount 3; mid-regen 2; after failed regen page turns 3, store turnCount 2, chunks 0000=1+2, note 'saved 12:25 PM', page summary back to old text. No busy check on the settings handler (2476).
findings.fix: Keep the old turn in adv.turns until the replacement commits (or block persist and edits while busy) so the intermediate state is never serialised.

findings.title: A reply cut off twice is committed as a normal turn with no visible warning
findings.summary: When both attempts hit the output cap, the repaired partial JSON is committed as a full turn and the status line is cleared; nothing the player sees says the reply was cut.
findings.scenario: The narrative ends mid-word, no suggestion buttons render, no events/beats/facts reach memory, state_updates after the cut are lost, and the clock advances by the default 15 minutes; the only record is the engine notes, visible only in spoiler mode.
findings.evidence: Status hidden; narrative ends ' You cross th'; suggestion buttons 0; events added 0; notes 'second reply was cut off by the runtime; used what could be repaired', 'only 0 suggestions returned', 'time_advance missing; used 15'; no warn pill without spoilers.
findings.fix: If the second reply is also truncated, fail the turn (rolling back) or require narrative plus suggestions and show a visible warning offering Regenerate.

findings.title: Memory fold and length fit accept any utility-model reply (refusal, truncated text, preamble, 3,000 words)
findings.summary: foldBeats replaces the summary with whatever text comes back, then permanently discards the 18 beats and 20 facts it was meant to merge. fitLength results are checked only for more than 50 words, and res.truncated is never read.
findings.scenario: A quick-tier refusal, truncated or one-word reply becomes the whole long-term summary and the folded beats are gone from memory and later prompts; a truncated fit, one with a 'Here's the rewritten passage:' preamble, or one longer than the input becomes the committed narrative.
findings.evidence: M.summary = s; if (foldBeatsNow) M.beats = M.beats.slice(18); and if (wc(fitted) > 50) { out.narrative = fitted }. Observed: summary now "I'm sorry, but I can't help with that request.", beats 43 -> 25; also summary 'Done.'; fit note 'length fitted 900 -> 3000 words'; truncated fit accepted.
findings.fix: Reject fold or fit results that are truncated, outside a sane length window (summary roughly 40-400 words, fit within the band) or refusal-shaped, and keep the old summary and narrative.

findings.title: Async handlers lack in-flight guards: double-click Undo removes two turns, double-click Take turn / Ctrl+Enter leaves a stale red banner, double OK / Begin re-enter
findings.summary: onUndo, onRegenerate and onSend check busy before awaiting syncFromStore(), and syncFromStore() returns false (carry on) when re-entered while syncing, so a second click passes the guard while the first is awaiting the db read. Ctrl+Enter ignores the disabled Take turn button; the inline OK and Begin buttons are re-enterable too.
findings.scenario: With a realistic db round trip, a double-click on Undo pops two turns (3 -> 1, stored turnCount 1) and issues overlapping writes; with one turn left the second click throws a TypeError. A double-click on Take turn, or Ctrl+Enter during a turn, leaves a red 'A turn is already running.' after the turn succeeds; without sample it replaces the banner holding the Retry button. A double-click on Begin is read as 'Begin now' and aborts all six invention calls after 0.1 s.
findings.evidence: probe_eng_7 (150 ms db, clicks 40 ms apart): turns 4 -> 2, store turnCount 2, overlapping-writes violations; Take turn: final status 'A turn is already running.' [bad]; probe_ui_30 (120 ms): 'before turns 3 -> after double-click Undo turns 1', with one turn TypeError reading 'stateBefore' at onUndo; probe_rend_9/9b: Ctrl+Enter -> Retry button gone / red banner persists; probe_rend_7: double Begin 'stopped after 0.1 s; 0 of 5 kept' x6; probe_rend_12: 6 unhandled {code:'aborted'}; probe_cr_2 pt3: 2nd Begin click made 0 invention calls.
findings.repro: probes/probe_eng_7.js, probe_eng_16.js (case 5), probe_ui_30.js, probe_rend_9.js, probe_rend_9b.js, probe_rend_7.js, probe_rend_12.js
findings.fix: Set a synchronous in-flight flag at the top of onUndo/onRegenerate/onSend/OK/Begin before any await and clear it in finally; gate Ctrl+Enter on busy and sample; make a re-entered syncFromStore make the caller bail rather than proceed; ignore a Begin re-click for ~1 s.

findings.title: Stop is shown but inert during the roommate introduction and memory fold, and Stop during length fit still commits the turn
findings.summary: Stop only aborts the shared ctl: writeRoommateIntro() sets busy and shows Stop but has no controller and passes no signal, foldBeats() passes no signal, and a cancelled fitLength() is caught and ignored by commitReply(), which goes on to commit the turn and clear the status without 'Stopped.'.
findings.scenario: After Begin on Sundered the page locks Take turn and shows 'Writing your roommate on the complex tier...' with a visible Stop that does nothing for 5-60+ s (a stalled call cannot be escaped without reloading); Stop during 'folding memory' commits the turn and replaces the summary; Stop during 'fitting length' saves the overlong unfitted turn.
findings.evidence: probe_rend_5 / probe_rt_2 / probe_ui_25: Stop clicked mid-intro, Stop stays visible, sample() received no signal, call stays pending, Take turn disabled; probe_rend_18 / probe_rt_10 / probe_ui_13 / probe_eng_6(B): Stop during fit -> turn committed, note 'length fit failed: cancelled', status cleared; probe_eng_6 / probe_ui_14: fold-stop beats 42 -> 25 and Stop ignored.
findings.repro: probes/probe_rend_5.js, probe_rend_18.js, probe_rt_2.js, probe_rt_10.js, probe_eng_6.js, probe_ui_25.js, probe_ui_13.js, probe_ui_14.js
findings.fix: Give writeRoommateIntro and foldBeats an AbortController tied to Stop and rethrow 'cancelled' after a cancelled fit/fold so takeTurn rolls the turn back.

findings.title: 60 s page-side invention timer also counts consent and queue time, and Begin fires six simultaneous batch calls
findings.summary: inventCall starts a 60 s setTimeout (INVENT_TIMEOUT_MS) before the db read and before the runtime has admitted the call; sample.d.ts says not to build a timeout because it counts the viewer's time on the consent dialog and queue wait. inventAll sends six batches (28 slots / 5) at once, plus a lingering player-invention call; whether this trips rate_limited could not be verified.
findings.scenario: With the runtime running about two calls at once, batches 5 and 6 wait ~45 s in the queue and are aborted at 60 s after ~15 s of work; a viewer who takes over 60 s on the first-call consent dialog likewise loses every call. The cast silently falls back to pool draws (visible only in Debug) and an invent_timeout failure doc is written per call.
findings.evidence: sample.d.ts: 'There is no timeout option and you should not build one'. probe_cr_11 (runtime concurrency 2, 22 s per call): '5/6: no reply in 60 s ... 0 received; 0 of 5 kept', 6/6 likewise; probe_rt_4 (concurrency 2, 25 s): 4/6, 5/6, 6/6 'no reply in 60 s', only 3 of 6 batches kept, Begin finished after 60.4 s; probe_ui_31 (calls held 65 s): six 'no reply in 60 s ... 0 of 5 kept'; probe_eng_21 (timer scaled): 7 calls cancelled; probe_p1_4: 5x Randomise + Begin = 12 pending calls.
findings.repro: probes/probe_cr_11.js, probe_cr_2.js, probe_rt_4.js, probe_rt_6.js, probe_ui_31.js, probe_eng_21.js, probe_p1_4.js
findings.fix: Drop the page-side timer (keep the user-driven Begin now and Stop) or start it at the first onText, and cap invention concurrency at about two batches (or ask for the cast in fewer calls).

findings.title: Player invention fires a model call with no viewer action (including on page load), superseded calls are never aborted, and a declined or disabled sample is never latched off
findings.summary: openCreate() calls randomAll(), which calls inventPlayerFields(), so every dialog open (including the automatic first-run open at boot) and every 'Randomise everything' makes a consent-triggering sample call with a random-seeded, never-stable prompt. The call has no external AbortSignal, so reroll, preset, Begin or Cancel only discards the result; after not_granted or sampling_disabled the page keeps calling and keeps showing 'Claude ready'.
findings.scenario: A first-time viewer with no saves gets the consent prompt at page load for a call they did not request; declining makes every later dialog open, Randomise press (1 call each) and Begin (6 calls) re-ask and fail while the header says Claude ready. Pressing Randomise everything three times leaves four concurrent player-invention calls (each up to 60 s), which then queue the six Begin batches behind them (peak concurrency 7).
findings.evidence: probe_cr_1: 1 sample call before any user action ('Invent the people...', 3889 B); probe_cr_2: after 3 clicks total sample calls 4, active 4, signals aborted [false x4]; probe_rt_1 case B: sampleCalls at load 1 [not_granted], after 3x Randomise + Begin 11 calls all not_granted, connText stays Claude ready; probe_rend_2: peak concurrency 7 after Begin, reopening dialog 3x = 3 calls; probe_p1_4: 12 pending, 0 aborted.
findings.repro: probes/probe_cr_1.js, probe_cr_2.js, probe_rt_1.js (case B), probe_rend_2.js, probe_p1_4.js
findings.fix: Invent the player's fields only on an explicit button press (or at Begin) with one AbortController aborted on reroll, preset, close and Begin; on not_granted/sampling_disabled set sample = null and show the bad connection state once.

findings.title: No window.claude (saved copy or other host) or a declined sample leaves the UI on 'connecting' / 'Claude ready' with no message
findings.summary: connectSample() and the boot IIFE call window.claude.use() unguarded; with no window.claude both reject with a TypeError (unhandled), so no status, no 'Claude unavailable' state and no creation dialog appears. 'Claude ready' is set as soon as use('sample') returns a function and no hide-class code (not_granted, sampling_disabled, not_declared, capability_*) ever changes it.
findings.scenario: A saved .html copy or top-level host shows the default world, a permanent 'connecting' badge, disabled Send and an empty status line, with no saves-unavailable note. If the viewer declines consent (or the org disables sampling) every call rejects not_granted but the header says Claude ready and Take turn stays live.
findings.evidence: probe_cr_1 H10: has claude? false | conn text 'connecting' | status '' hidden | send disabled | 2 unhandled 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading use)'; probe_rend_3 same, use()->null variant handled; probe_p1_3, probe_rt_1 case A likewise; probe_rend_14: all calls not_granted -> header 'Claude ready', Take turn enabled, each turn 'not allowed'.
findings.repro: probes/probe_cr_1.js, probe_rend_3.js, probe_rend_14.js, probe_p1_3.js, probe_rt_1.js (case A)
findings.fix: Guard on window.claude && window.claude.use (try/catch) and take the existing 'Claude unavailable' / 'saves unavailable' path; on hide-class codes set the header to bad, disable sample-dependent controls and show a persistent banner.

findings.title: Cast editor Save corrupts name fields: first becomes the title, last goes stale, renames never reach {npc_*} references
findings.summary: saveCast always sets first: name.split(' ')[0], which is the title ('Dean', 'Professor', 'Dr') for titled cast, and never updates last. vars() resolves {npc_key} from adv.cast.generated (the base list), ignoring cast.overrides, so a rename does not propagate into other characters' sheets although the code comment claims it will.
findings.scenario: Pressing Save on the Dean without any change writes override first='Dean', so an action naming the Dean's real first name yields 'Focus: the action names Dean'; renaming the Dean leaves the Historian's sheet saying 'Knows ..., Dean <old surname>', so the narrator sees two different people.
findings.evidence: probe_cr_4: after unchanged Save override.dean.first = 'Dean' (generated first = 'Ravepey'); probe_cr_20: before 'Focus: the action names Calanthe', after unchanged Save 'Focus: the action names Dean'; probe_cr_5: historian sheet still 'Knows Elowen Mossback, Dean Vespera Ashcombe' after renaming Dean to 'Dean Zed Quux'.
findings.fix: Only overwrite first/last when the name actually changed, deriving them without the title, and build vars() from activeCharacters() so overrides apply.

findings.title: 'Reset to the world's version' does nothing for the roommate yet reports success; Reset and Remove leave a renamed character wrongly matched in state.present
findings.summary: saveCast edits the roommate in place (Object.assign(adv.roommate, ...)) rather than via cs.overrides, but resetCast only deletes cs.overrides[castSel], so Reset is a no-op for the roommate and the list never shows the edit marker. Reset on any renamed character leaves the renamed entry in state.present, and toggleRemoveCast filters state.present by the base name, so a renamed character stays present. A blank attitude field is saved as 0.
findings.scenario: The player renames the roommate, clicks Reset: the form still shows the edited name while the note says 'Back to the world's version.' and the original is unrecoverable from the UI. After resetting or removing a renamed NPC (Marisol -> 'Zed Edited') the character is no longer matched or stays in Present.
findings.evidence: probe_cr_4: after save list entry 'Renamed Roommate (Bovine mythkin) | cfNote Saved.' then after Reset cfName = Renamed Roommate | cfNote 'Back to the world's version.'; probe_ui_8: stored name unchanged, attitude '' -> 0; probe_ui_34: present after Remove ['Iavemjj','Corin Blake','Zed Edited'], hidden ['marisol'].
findings.fix: Keep the roommate's generated original (or route roommate edits through cs.overrides) so Reset can restore it, map state.present back on reset, filter present by displayed name and aliases, and treat a blank attitude as unchanged.

findings.title: Cast editor 'Aim' and 'Usually found' edits are silently ignored whenever the character has slot-specific text
findings.summary: buildPrompt prefers where[slot] / aims[slot] over .default, but the Cast editor writes only .default and labels it 'any time of day'. Almost every cast member has evening/night/class slot entries.
findings.scenario: The player edits a character's Aim or Where and saves; in the evening (and at night for Where) the narrator still receives the authored text, so the edit appears to do nothing for much of the day.
findings.evidence: Real UI run: saved Where='...EDITED-WHERE', Aim='EDITED-AIM'; 08:00 and 12:30 applied; 19:30: where applied false, aim applied false; 23:30: where false, aim true. Label reads 'Aim (default, any time of day)'.
findings.repro: probes/probe_c1_castedit.js (and probe_c1_where.js for slot keys per character)
findings.fix: When saving, also overwrite or clear the slot-specific entries, or show an editor per slot; at minimum fix the 'any time of day' label.

findings.title: Lore keys match as raw substrings, so short keys fire on ordinary words ('ring', 'bet', 'tree', 'war', 'pack', 'cow', 'spa', 'pen', 'Hale', 'salt')
findings.summary: Bare keys use hay.includes(kk) with no word boundary (only '*' keys get \b), so 3-4 letter keys in all three worlds trigger on substrings of unrelated words; the spurious entries are species/Spa/reach-salt entries of priority 6-9 and ~800-1,100 rendered chars, crowding out relevant lore.
findings.scenario: In every default Sundered game the opening's own text ('half-unpacked', 'stringing', 'ledge') pulls in wolf, fairy and Edge lore on turns 1-3; 'morning/during/bring' triggers fairy, 'between' fox, 'street' dryad, 'toward' Sundering, 'space' the Mythaven Restoration Spa entry, 'Unpack first' wolf; in Halloway 'exhale' pulls Hale, 'shallow water' low water, 'open' pen, 'Pass the salt' the reach-salt plot (names Bram Ostler).
findings.evidence: Real activeLore(): 'Mara is bringing the morning tea during the walk between classes.' -> fairy(ring), fox(bet); 'down the street toward the warm kitchen' -> dryad(tree), Sundering(war); 'coward ... scowl' -> cow; 'backpack' -> wolf(pack). Halloway: opening -> [pen, town, register, low water]; 'exhale' -> Hale; 'finished' -> shed; 'flights' -> lights; 'ravenous' -> raven; 'Pass the salt' -> reach-salt. Mythaven plain-English hits for ring, bet, tree, spa, cream, pack, cat, nap, lap, elm.
findings.fix: Match bare keys as whole words (\bkey\b, keeping '*' for prefixes), make phrase-only keys explicit ('fairy ring', 'Dr Hale', 'the pens'), and audit short keys (ring, bet, tree, war, pack, cow, nap, lap, sap, pen, inn, shed, spa, salt).

findings.title: focusNames fires on surnames/aliases that are ordinary words (Fell, Salt, Marrow, Hazel, Vane, Pike, Marsh) and shared surnames, issuing a false 'Focus' directive
findings.summary: Handles (surnames, aliases, first names) are matched case-insensitively as whole words, so common words in ordinary prose select a cast member, and surnames shared with others (Ambergill vs Ambergill-Vey, Reyes sisters) also match. The prompt then states the turn belongs to that character and that nobody else arrives and nothing interrupts.
findings.scenario: Mythaven 'I fell asleep on the stairs' tells the narrator the action names Professor Fell, 'I pass the salt to Marisol' adds Nerissa Salt, 'I ask Professor Ambergill-Vey about the mirror' locks onto Pip, 'I ask Yuki Reyes about the bet' onto Tamsin; narration containing 'fell' or 'salt' pulls those full sheets. Generated Sundered casts draw surnames such as Fell and Marsh from pools, so it applies there too.
findings.evidence: Real prompt: 'Focus: the action names Fell, so the turn belongs to them: reaching them, being with them, what they say and do; nobody else arrives and nothing interrupts unless the action invites it.' 'marrow in the soup bone' -> Marrow; 'I draw a salt line' -> Nerissa; 'weather vane' -> Kestrel; 'order the pike' -> Jonah.
findings.fix: Match handles case-sensitively against the original action (names are capitalised), skip handles that are common words or prefixes of other names; in the world rename Fell, Salt, Vane, Pike and give Pip a surname that is not a prefix of 'Ambergill-Vey'.

findings.title: Halloway premise starts with 'You are {name}', so the creation dialog shows a raw {name} and the invention prompt carries the wrong world's text and another adventure's player name
findings.summary: premiseParts() splits only at '. You are ', which the other worlds' premises contain after a setting sentence; Halloway's premise begins 'You are {name}', so the whole unfilled premise becomes 'setting' and is written into #cPremise, and inventPrompt fills it from the ALREADY LOADED adventure's player. inventPrompt also hard-codes Mythaven's curriculum ('The university teaches Glamour, Applied Alchemy ...', empty '()' lists, 'in the manner of: .').
findings.scenario: Choosing Halloway in New adventure shows 'You are {name}, nineteen, a first-year at Halloway...'; the player-invention call is told 'Setting: You are Alex Rowan/Nova Pike (another adventure's player), nineteen, a first-year at Halloway...' plus a university course rule, so invented names and personalities can bleed Mythaven/Sundered content into Halloway. Invented backgrounds likewise appear with a literal {first}.
findings.evidence: probe_c1_halcreate: cPremise "You are {name}, nineteen, a first-year at Halloway College of Binding..."; probe_cr_8 prompt: 'Setting: You are Alex Rowan, nineteen...' and 'course: ... The university teaches Glamour, Applied Alchemy, Artificing, Wardcraft and Sigils ... ();'; probe_ph_13, probe_hw_2, probe_hw_7, probe_ui_21/_22 agree.
findings.repro: probes/probe_c1_halcreate.js, probe_cr_8.js, probe_ph_7.js, probe_ph_13.js, probe_hw_2.js, probe_hw_7.js, probe_ui_21.js, probe_ui_22.js
findings.fix: Open the premise with a setting sentence (moving 'You are {name}...' after '. ' as in mythaven.js:12) or split on /^You are |\. You are /, fill the setting with the creation world's own default player, and emit the course rule only when Wc.genPools.courses exists.

findings.title: The personal opening paragraph is stored and sent to the narrator but never shown to the player
findings.summary: openingNarrative() prepends the premise's personal part ('You are <name>, nineteen, human...') to adv.opening.narrative, but openingTurn() (documented as 'Turn 0 for the prompt') strips it and renderFeed displays that stripped text; the creation dialog shows only the setting half.
findings.scenario: In Mythaven and Sundered the player never reads who they are, the scholarship, the Sundering line or 'This evening is the cross-species mixer...' (story starts at 'Room 4B is at the top of Kettle Hall...'), yet the narrator holds it in <world> (and rule 6 says the character knows only what the player has read). Halloway is unaffected.
findings.evidence: probe_rend_1: Sundered saved opening 1956 chars starting 'You are Pavemjj Sorrowxim, nineteen, human. Three weeks ago...', shown Turn 0 1370 chars starting 'Room 4B...'; Mythaven 2127 vs 1581. probe_c1_opening: feed contains it? false, anywhere in document text? false, prompt contains it? true. probe_sw_4 likewise (one reviewer was unsure the strip is intended).
findings.fix: Render adv.opening.narrative (plus the 'before' block) in renderFeed and keep openingTurn() for buildPrompt and the lastLine in advDoc only.

findings.title: Day-1-only schedule rows recur every Monday: 'orientation (no classes on Day 1)' in the authoritative <clock> and a recurring orientation mixer in Coming days
findings.summary: The entry '10:00 orientation (no classes on Day 1)' is recurring (days: Monday) and Day 1 starts at 17:40, so it only ever fires on later Mondays; the 19:00 entry 'the mixer on the quad (orientation Monday); goblin night market ... (other Mondays)' has no day filter, and calendarLine cuts names at the first ' (' or ',', so every future Monday reads as the orientation mixer.
findings.scenario: On Day 8 (Monday) 10:30 the clock says 'Now: orientation (no classes on Day 1). Next: 12:00 lunch'; from Day 2 on the Coming days line announces 'the mixer on the quad 19:00' every Monday instead of the goblin night market, and Tuesday shows only the Moonrunners run, never the Sigil Circle. The narrator must treat the authoritative clock as truth.
findings.evidence: probe_c1_clock: 'Day 8, Monday, 10:30. Now: orientation (no classes on Day 1). Next: 12:00 lunch, dining hall.'; probe_st_20: 'Day 8 Monday 10:30 => Now: orientation (no classes on Day 1)'; Coming days 'Day 8 Monday (Glamour Theory 09:00; Artificing workshop 13:00; the mixer on the quad 19:00)' in both Mythaven and Sundered; probe_mwd_2 (Mythaven Day 8 and Day 5 clock).
findings.fix: Remove the orientation row and split the 19:00 entry into a Day-1-only mixer and a recurring Monday market (or add a day field the engine honours); do not truncate names at ' (' or ',' when alternatives follow.

findings.title: Evening aims and where.free written for the Day-1 mixer are applied to every evening of every week
findings.lines: worlds/mythaven.js:281-343, 397-457 (aims.evening, wolf where.free, cow where.class2), 455-457; worlds/sundered.js:79,94,100,103,106,112-113,167,181,248,274,289 (aims.evening), 635; index.html:1303-1306
findings.summary: buildPrompt picks where[slot] / aims[slot] by slot name only, and the 'evening' slot recurs every night, yet the evening aims of creamery, library, gardener, warren, stall, human_society, cory, hazel, priya, ilse, pip, bexley, marisol and most roommate species describe Day 1's mixer (or a one-off rivalry goal); the wolf roommate's where.free applies at the 17:40 opening although the roommate is in room 4B, and the cow's class2 applies all five weekdays.
findings.scenario: On Day 4/5/9 evenings the narrator is told Cory's aim is to 'skip the mixer', Hazel's to 'watch the mixer from the edge of the quad', Priya's to give the leaflet 'at the mixer', the Sundered stall goblin to strike a bargain and the warren rabbit to find the player 'at the mixer'; human_society's where reads 'the mixer only to hand out leaflets' on other nights, and Turn 1 says 'Now: the Moon Field' while state.present puts the wolf in 4B. The narrator is pushed to restage a one-night event.
findings.evidence: Mythaven Day 5 Thursday 20:00: cory 'Aim now: skip the mixer'; hazel 'watch the mixer from the edge of the quad'; marisol 'press a cocoa on Mavemjj at the mixer'; priya 'find Mavemjj at the mixer and give her the Society leaflet and a warning'; Day 9 Mon 20:00 wolf roommate 'keep the pack from crowding Zavemjj at the mixer'; Sundered Day 4 Thu 20:10: creamery/stall/warren aims 'at the mixer'.
findings.fix: Make aims.evening event-neutral and carry mixer-night aims in the opening beats or facts, give the wolf no where.free (or 'room 4B or the Moon Field'), add an 'otherwise' place to human_society's where.evening, and optionally let the engine key aims on weekday as well as slot.

findings.title: Mythaven rules still carry Sundered Isle setting text (cliff path, cloud below, cloud ferry, bricked doors, closed places)
findings.summary: Rule 'Setting texture' (line 31, copied from worlds/sundered.js:36) tells the narrator 'The Isle is real ground with an edge: a rail on the cliff path, cloud instead of sea below ... a ferry out of the cloud twice a day' and cites 'the old wall with its bricked doors'; 'Length and detail' (line 22) cites 'a closed place opening'. None exists in Mythaven (wooded lake campus outside a human city, no dungeons; player arrives 'by the inland bus').
findings.scenario: Every Mythaven prompt carries these phrases, steering the narrator to put cliff rails, cloud below and a cloud ferry beside a lakeshore campus and to use bricked doors and closed places the world never defines; it contradicts world[0] (line 42) and the 'contradict nothing in <facts>' rule cannot resolve it.
findings.evidence: Built Mythaven prompt contains 'ferry out of the cloud', 'cloud instead of sea', 'bricked doors', 'a closed place opening' (all true), W has dungeons? false; debug prompt <rules> quote. memorySeed: 'arrives at Mythaven University by the inland bus'.
findings.fix: Rewrite line 31 for the lake campus (lake weather, the road or bus to the city) and delete 'a closed place opening' from line 22; replace or define 'a lake town' in the Themes rule (line 26).

findings.title: Typed (custom) or non-binary roommate gets broken intro text: 'they says', 'they does', 'Looks: .', 'a elf'
findings.summary: A species with no pool has no looks, so the plain intro prints ', basilisk from the first glance, and plainly.' and the narrator prompt contains 'Looks: .'. The intros hard-code the verb after the pronoun ('{rm_they} says', 'does not explain') without the {rm_s}/{rm_es} tokens, giving 'they says'/'they does' for non-binary roommates, and the prompt writes 'a ' + kind ('a elf'). This player-facing text is Turn 0 because template roommates are never rewritten.
findings.scenario: Sundered, type Basilisk with a non-binary roommate and let the intro fall back: '...doorway, basilisk from the first glance, and plainly. "Ellis," they says.' Mythaven _generic intro (any typed species, e.g. Troll): 'they does not explain and does not need to. "Bran," they says.' With sample on, the intro prompt for Elf has 'Looks: .' so the narrator gets no body description. A drawn Sundered Siren non-binary gives '"Vale," they says.'
findings.evidence: probe_mw_5: 'Troll, second-year, plainly; they does not explain ... "Bran," they says.'; probe_ph_2: 'stops in the doorway, basilisk from the first glance, and plainly. "Ellis," they says.'; probe_ph_11: prompt 'Looks: .' and "arm's reach of a elf with no glamour on"; probe_wd_16: '"Vale," they says.'
findings.repro: probes/probe_mw_5.js, probe_ph_2.js (sundered female Basilisk nonbinary), probe_ph_11.js, probe_ph_4.js, probe_wd_16.js
findings.fix: Use agreement tokens in the intros ('{rm_they} say{rm_s}', 'do{rm_es}'), give custom species a looks fallback or drop the Looks clause, and choose a/an from the first letter.

findings.title: Typed roommate species is matched by substring, so unrelated words get a species template ('Chimera'/'Merlin' -> Merfolk, 'Coward' -> Bovine, 'a' -> Harpy)
findings.summary: matchRoommateSpecies accepts nm.includes(t) or t.includes(key/short) at any length, so short keys such as mer, cat, cow, fox and wolf match inside unrelated words and a single letter matches a species.
findings.scenario: Typing 'Chimera' (the Dean's own kind), 'Merlin' or 'Hammerhead' reports 'Full template: Merfolk' / 'Known species: Merfolk' and Begin builds a Merfolk roommate with gills; 'cattle' gives a cat, 'Coward' Bovine, 'Catfish' Cat, 'Cowardly lion' Bovine; the custom species is silently replaced.
findings.evidence: probe_ui_3: 'Chimera' -> 'Full template: Merfolk.'; 'Coward' -> Bovine mythkin; 'a' -> Harpy; probe_ui_4: Begin with 'Chimera' in Sundered -> 'roommate Tavemjj Dorrowxim (Merfolk)'; probe_wd_11/_13: 'cattle' -> Cat; probe_cr_12: 'Hammerhead shark' -> Merfolk.
findings.fix: Match only exact key/name/short (case-insensitive) or whole words and drop the nm.includes(t) branch.

findings.title: Clicking the 'Two things you are good at' label re-rolls the player's strengths
findings.summary: The Random button sits inside the field's <label> with no for attribute, so the label's control is that button and any click or tap on the caption (or the empty rest of its full-width row) fires Random; the checkbox group also has no group name.
findings.scenario: A player carefully picks two strengths and a weakness, then taps the caption: the choices change at random without any prompt and focus jumps to Random.
findings.evidence: <label>Two things you are good at <button data-rand="traits">Random</button></label>; Chromium label.control is the BUTTON; label.click() changed the checked set 'charm,vigour' -> 'nerve,charm' (6 clicks each changed it); a real mouse click changed 'charm,vigour | weak=nerve' to 'charm,empathy | wits'; the label is 843px wide.
findings.repro: Browser pane at http://127.0.0.1:4173/ (New adventure dialog; label.control, label.click())
findings.fix: Move the Random button out of the <label> and make the checks container a fieldset/legend or role=group with aria-labelledby.

findings.title: Creation dialog: stale roommate fields leak into other worlds' presets, and loadPresets has no stale-result guard
findings.summary: openCreate resets roommate fields only when the world has a roommate, so Halloway presets and their default name carry the previous world's species; loadPresets has no stale-result guard, so a late result for world A fills world B's dropdown.
findings.scenario: Halloway default preset name reads 'Bavemjj Worrowxim · Werewolf roommate'; the Halloway dialog lists 'My preset' saved in Sundered.
findings.evidence: probe_cr_14: Halloway default preset name 'Bavemjj Worrowxim · Werewolf roommate'; probe_cr_12: Halloway dialog lists 'My preset' saved in Sundered.
findings.fix: Clear roommate fields on every world change and guard loadPresets with a sequence token.

findings.title: Adventure id / persist(): not serialised, so quick repeated actions overlap writes to the same document
findings.summary: Undo, settings changes, Save summary, Override and Cast saves each call persist() without waiting for the previous one, and persist rewrites the adventure doc and chunk every time. The db contract allows one write at a time per document; an overlapping pair can land out of order or answer resource_exhausted.
findings.scenario: Double-clicking Undo (which also removes two turns), Save summary, or changing two Settings selects within one save round trip puts two set() calls on adventures/<id> and on the chunk doc in flight together, leaving the store one step behind the page until the next save.
findings.evidence: probe_p5_10 (dbLatency 40 ms): violations 'overlapping-writes: set adventures/<id> ... while another write to the same doc is in flight' and for turns/0000; probe_ps_11: same after double Save summary and two quick settings changes; probe_ui_19: for two setSel changes, a double Save summary and two attitude edits.
findings.fix: Queue persist() calls on one promise chain (coalescing pending ones) so a document never has two writes in flight.

findings.title: logFailure keys documents by Date.now() base36: same-millisecond failures collide, and records are filed under a never-saved or previous adventure
findings.summary: logFailure writes adventures/<id>/failures/<Date.now() base36> fire-and-forget, so six parallel invention failures in one millisecond write one document concurrently (overlapping-writes, last writer wins). Because Begin invents before newAdventure(), adv.id is the placeholder or previous adventure, leaving orphan docs; it also ignores input.tier/bytes from the timeout path, logs for every declined call, and nothing reads the docs back.
findings.scenario: A rate_limited flood on Begin yields 7 failed calls but only 2-4 stored records, plus overlapping-writes; surviving records sit under adventures/<placeholder>/failures with no parent doc, which the delete flow never removes and which spend the shared 5,000-document quota; a viewer who declines consent leaves docs the same way.
findings.evidence: probe_cr_10: failure docs 4 for 7 failed invention calls, violation 'overlapping-writes: set adventures/advmupw6hz6i36c/failures/mupw6ih8', parent absent from the adventures listing; probe_rt_6: 6 rate_limited, stored 2, 4 violations; probe_rt_1 B: 6 failure docs under placeholder id parentDoc=false; probe_ui_18; probe_ph_4 sundered composed.
findings.fix: Add a counter or random suffix to the failure doc id, skip db logging when no adventure is persisted or the code is not_granted/rate_limited, cap the log, and pass tier/bytes through extra.

findings.title: Failure-log documents are unbounded, deleting an adventure removes only 100 of them, and the list shows only 50 adventures
findings.summary: logFailure writes one document (up to 30,000 chars of raw text) per unusable reply (two per failed turn) with no cap, and the delete handler queries limit(100) once, so surplus docs are orphaned but still count against the 5,000-document quota. The list query is limit(50), so older adventures cannot be reached or deleted to free quota.
findings.scenario: After about 50-65 failed turns an adventure has 112-130 failure docs; deleting it leaves 12-30 orphans forever, and heavy use of a flaky tier slowly consumes the shared quota chunk creation also needs; a user with more than 50 saves cannot see or delete the oldest.
findings.evidence: probe_p5_12: 56 unusable replies -> 112 failure docs, orphans left 12; probe_ps_9 (H8): 130 docs after 65 failed turns, 30 leftover after Delete; 50-row cap static (1814).
findings.fix: Keep failures in one capped document or prune to the last ~20, loop the delete until the failures query is empty, and page the adventure list beyond 50.

findings.title: Boot: a failed adventures query reads as 'no saves yet', and the windlass.last fallback is dead
findings.summary: The boot-time newAdventure() writes its throwaway id into localStorage 'windlass.last' before line 2564 reads it, so the fallback can never find a real save; the swallowed catch on the ordered query then routes any query error to 'no saves yet' and opens the create dialog. Boot also tries only the single most recent save and does not fall back to the next one when it fails to load.
findings.scenario: A transient 'unavailable' on the adventures query for a player with saves shows 'no saves yet' and the New adventure dialog; the save is reachable via Adventures but the player is told it does not exist. If the newest save has an unknown world id, boot reports a load failure and shows a fresh adventure.
findings.evidence: probe_p5_1: LS last was the real id, after boot 'windlass.last' = throwaway id; note 'no saves yet', create dialog open true; probe_ps_1: '[boot query transient fail] note: no saves yet | create dialog open: true | last= <throwaway id>'; '[unknown world] note: could not load saves: world ghostworld is not loaded'.
findings.fix: Read windlass.last before the first newAdventure() (or skip writing it for an unsaved adventure), retry the query once, show 'could not load saves: <code>' on failure, and fall back to the next save when the newest cannot load.

findings.title: Unsaved edits in the Summary box are silently overwritten by the next render
findings.summary: renderRail() resets #summary from adv.memory.summary whenever the box is not focused, and nothing marks an edit as unsaved.
findings.scenario: A player edits the summary to steer the narrator, clicks into the action box and takes a turn: renderAll() puts the stored text back, so the edit vanishes and the turn used the old summary. Only an explicit Save summary click keeps it.
findings.evidence: probe_rend_8 (a): set #summary='MY EDITED SUMMARY (not saved yet)', focus #action, take a turn -> value reverted to the stored summary.
findings.fix: Track a dirty flag on input and skip the reset while dirty, or save the summary on blur and before Take turn.

findings.title: Failure of a Regenerate/turn flow: success clears the action and director boxes the player was drafting
findings.summary: takeTurn clears #action and #director on success without checking whether the turn is a regeneration.
findings.scenario: Player types the next action and a director note, then presses Regenerate on the last turn: when it finishes both boxes are empty and the draft is lost.
findings.evidence: hideDraft(); renderAll(); $('#action').value = ''; $('#director').value = ''; runs for regen turns too. Observed 'my next action draft' / 'my next director draft' -> '' / '' after Regenerate.
findings.fix: Clear the boxes only when opts.regen is not set.

findings.title: Valid JSON without a narrative is never retried and the error says 'twice'; non-object JSON surfaces as a page error
findings.summary: The one automatic retry fires only when the reply cannot be parsed, so {}, {"error":...} or {"narrative":""} fail after one call while the message claims two; a top-level number, string or true reaches normaliseReply and crashes on the 'in' operator.
findings.scenario: One sample call followed by 'The reply was not usable, twice.'; for a reply of 5, 'hello there' or true: "Page error: Cannot use 'in' operator to search for 'exposures' in 5 (see Debug)." and no retry.
findings.evidence: if (!data) { ... second ask } only; commitReply: if (!out.narrative) throw { code: 'invalid_json' } after the first reply; for (const k of TURN_KEYS) if (!(k in d)). Observed calls=1 for 6 such shapes.
findings.fix: Treat a parsed value that is not an object with a non-empty string narrative as unusable and retry once; word the message from the real attempt count.

findings.title: At 150 s the page says it is still waiting for the first word even when text has been streaming
findings.summary: The elapsed-time ticker raises 'Still waiting for the first word after 150 s' unconditionally at s === 150 without checking whether onText has fired; it also counts the consent-dialog wait.
findings.scenario: A slow but healthy turn (long write, fit, fold) shows 'writing...' from 4 s, then a red 'Still waiting for the first word... You can Stop and try again.', which can make the player abort a turn that is progressing.
findings.evidence: if (s === 150) setStatus('Still waiting for the first word after 150 s. You can Stop and try again.', true). Scaled x20 run: 'writing...' at 4 s, then at 151 s that message [bad] while the draft was streaming; probe_ui_29 agrees.
findings.repro: probes/probe_eng_12.js (performance.now and setInterval scaled x20), probe_ui_29.js
findings.fix: Raise the message only while no text has arrived (share the first-text flag with the timer) and clear it on first text.

findings.title: Null or non-string model values leak as '[object Object]', 'null' and 'undefined', and null/empty coercion corrupts numbers, flags and time
findings.summary: normaliseReply maps entries with String(), and applyUpdates builds present from String(val), uses Number(val) (null/'' -> 0), tests booleans only for lowercase 'false', and the attitude inc path uses (Number(current) || prev) so a legitimate 0 is replaced; time_advance_minutes null or '' advances the clock by 0 with no note.
findings.scenario: suggested_actions [{text}, null, 3] render buttons '[object Object]', 'null', '3'; events [{...}] are stored as '[object Object]' and resent in every later <timeline>; present set with null gives ['null']; attitudes.roommate set to null moves 5 -> 4; curfew_strikes set null/'' resets 2 -> 0; flags 'False'/'no'/'0' stay true; quill prev 1 inc -1,-1,+1 ends at 2.
